questions.question: Apple employees are not allowed to correct customers if they mispronounce product names.
questions.answer: True - Apple emphasizes customer experience and avoids creating discomfort or embarrassment.

questions.question: Starbucks employees are required to taste-test all coffee products daily to ensure quality.
questions.answer: False - While tasting is encouraged during training, daily testing is not required for all products.

questions.question: Zappos pays $3,000 to employees if they quit after a brief training period.
questions.answer: True - Zappos offers this bonus to ensure only motivated employees stay.

questions.question: At Tesla, employees must wear blue socks to demonstrate company unity.
questions.answer: False - There is no known sock color policy at Tesla.

questions.question: Microsoft banned drinking non-caffeinated beverages in the office to maintain productivity.
questions.answer: False - Microsoft has no official rule banning non-caffeinated drinks.

questions.question: The New York Yankees had a no-beard policy for all male employees.
questions.answer: True - The Yankees enforce a strict grooming policy that prohibits facial hair beyond mustaches.

questions.question: At Disney World, employees had to share undergarments for character costumes until 2001.
questions.answer: True - This policy existed until union complaints led to changes in costume hygiene practices.

questions.question: American Apparel employees were hired or fired based on their physical attractiveness.
questions.answer: True - The company was known for strict aesthetic standards in hiring practices.

questions.question: A UK company introduced 'Naked Fridays' where employees could work nude.
questions.answer: True - This unusual initiative was tried as a team-building experiment in 2009.

questions.question: All Google employees must wear a badge indicating their favorite snack for instant bonding.
questions.answer: False - This is not an official policy at Google.
